objective: Add provider-neutral trace-segment checkpoint receipts that bind ordered trace spans to lifecycle checkpoints, event counts, flush/cancellation boundaries, sensitive-data policy, generation, replay-safe resume evidence, and non-authority semantics without exporting traces or executing work.

research_inputs.finding: The current memory tool is client-side and the application controls storage, path restrictions, and returned tool results; just-in-time retrieval avoids loading all persistent memory into active context.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL binds trace checkpoint receipts to caller-supplied lifecycle/state digests and keeps storage/export outside the contract.

research_inputs.finding: Long-running agents require durable progress artifacts, clean incremental commits, explicit continuity across context windows, and end-to-end verification; compaction alone is insufficient.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL adds ordered trace-segment continuity and replay-safe resume evidence adjacent to task lifecycle and checkpoint receipts.

research_inputs.finding: Current agent tracing records nested task, turn, generation, tool, guardrail, handoff, and custom spans, with immediate flush support and configurable sensitive-data capture.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL binds span sequence, flush status, cancellation boundary, and sensitive-data policy digest into deterministic checkpoint receipts without exporting traces.

research_inputs.finding: MCP supports progress, cancellation, error reporting, durable Tasks, and explicit user consent/control; tool descriptions remain untrusted.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: The contract rejects unacknowledged cancellation boundaries and keeps trace/checkpoint data explicitly non-authoritative.

features: ordered span and segment sequence continuity
lifecycle checkpoint and objective-state digest binding

limitations: The module emits checkpoint evidence but does not export traces, flush provider backends, access tracing dashboards, execute work, or validate external lifecycle state.
Span payload, lifecycle checkpoint, objective state, and sensitive-data policy digests are caller-supplied evidence and require independent trusted instrumentation for production trust.
A flushed status is a supplied status; it does not prove a remote exporter durably stored data unless an external exporter attests it.
The benchmark measures local Python receipt overhead and excludes model, network, trace-export, browser, tool, accelerator, storage, and kernel scheduling latency.
The real held-out evaluation uses deterministic fixture adapters and does not measure trace-segment efficacy, browser autonomy, robotics, frontier models, or general intelligence.
No physical accelerator, TPM, secure enclave, production KMS, independent builder, live multihost deployment, or external security review was exercised.
This evidence does not claim AGI capability, production approval, superiority to Linux, or closure of existing external release blockers.
